abstract: Drago and Laine argue advanced AI could trigger an 'intelligence curse' analogous to the resource curse: states and firms that capture frontier capability concentrate economic and political power, weaken incentives to invest in human capital, and hollow out broad-based economic participation. The piece reads as a warning against laissez-faire AI deployment from a labor-share standpoint.
keyFindings: Frames AI capability as a quasi-natural-resource whose concentrated capture corrodes broader institutions
Predicts weakening of human-capital investment incentives in AI-rich economies
Argues for governance and redistributive mechanisms that prevent capability monopolization
Adopted in some labor-economics and political-economy circles as a structural risk framing
methodology: Essay drawing on resource-curse economics and AI capability concentration trends; not an empirical estimate.
qualifiers: Tier 3 essay. Authors not in mainstream academic labor economics; the resource-curse analogy is contested. Useful as a position to cite alongside more empirically anchored work.
